 Jason must recover a seized vehicle from a police impound in Hamlet during Unwanted Attention, a Chapter 1 mission in Grand Theft Auto 6. The mission introduces police radio scanning, vehicle theft, evasion mechanics, and appearance changes that help players avoid law enforcement.
 According to walkthroughs published by Video Games Chronicle, GTA BOOM, and Eurogamer between November 18 and 19, 2026, the mission becomes available alongside other activities after players complete Gone Fishing.
 Advertisement 
 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 Players begin by meeting Cal Hampton near his pickup truck at the northern end of Key Lento. After speaking with him, Jason drives to the police impound on Penny Bun Street in Hamlet. Cal installs a police scanner on Jason's phone, allowing him to monitor police radio communications.
 Also Read 
 GTA 6 Locks Two Strip Clubs Behind Story Progress 
 The main objective is to retrieve a red Imponte '77 Phoenix from the impound yard. Cal sends a photograph of the target vehicle, helping players identify it among the other seized cars.
 According to Eurogamer, players can use the WAiNK application to scan vehicles and identify the correct car. The Phoenix is positioned near a tow truck beneath a metal awning. GTA BOOM also identifies it as a vehicle located behind a blue-and-white tow truck.
 Players must enter the restricted property by climbing over the perimeter or forcing an entrance. Forcing the gate triggers an alarm, while crouching and using parked vehicles for cover helps Jason move through the compound without attracting additional attention.
 Also Read 
 GTA 6 Crashes Prompt PS5 Troubleshooting Warnings 
 Once the Phoenix has been located, Jason must free it from its towing equipment, enter the vehicle, and start its engine. The escape triggers a police pursuit, making it necessary to break line of sight and leave the marked search area.
 GTA BOOM explains that players must align two indicators using the controller's analog sticks during the vehicle-starting sequence. The car must also remain operational throughout the escape, as excessive damage can cause mission failure.
 After escaping the immediate pursuit, Jason receives instructions from Brian to visit Pay 'N' Spray in Hamlet. Players can repair the vehicle free of charge during this mission and must select a noticeably different paint color before continuing.
 Also Read 
 Rockstar Launches GTA 6 Without Online Multiplayer 
 The original red paint may appear as a free option, but the game can display the warning "Too similar" when the selected color does not differ sufficiently from the existing finish.
 Changing the vehicle's appearance helps reduce police recognition. Players must then drive the Phoenix to Brian's storage facility and park it inside the open loading bay. GTA BOOM reports that completing this delivery rewards Jason with GTA$150.
 Jason must also reduce his personal recognition level by changing his appearance. Eurogamer recommends removing his hat and equipping glasses through the equipment menu, while GTA BOOM explains that players can remove existing accessories through the inventory interface.
 Also Read 
 GTA 6 Features Bobby Moynihan as Cal Hampton 
 Players are additionally directed to a nearby clothing store to purchase an outfit. Changing clothes is important because Jason's appearance contributes to his criminal recognition level, alongside his vehicle and other identifying characteristics.
 According to Eurogamer, the mission ends after Jason delivers the Phoenix to the storage facility and completes the required appearance changes. Subsequent available activities include Collect Brian's Rent (Lab Fees), Fix Your Car, and Pick Up A Gun, while Pipework is also assigned as Jason heads home.
